Container.Name: NASlab-Agent
Container.Overview:
Getting the app: NASlab is coming to the Google Play Store in the next few days. Until then it is in a closed test, see https://tuxxler.github.io/nzblab/en/#play Read-only monitoring agent for the NASlab Android app. It measures your server every 30 seconds (temperature sensors, CPU load, GPU usage, RAM, network, disk spin-ups and which programs caused them, top processes, cache usage per share) and keeps a file index for searching all shares. History: 8 days at full resolution, 2 years of hourly values, stored in /config.
Tested on Unraid 7 (amd64); arm64 is not tested yet.
It never changes anything on your server: every host path is mounted read-only, only /config is writable, root is dropped after start (PUID/PGID), and the container runs read-only with almost all capabilities removed. Optional and off by default: SMART values (NZBLAB_SMART), backup discovery for extra paths (NZBLAB_BACKUP_PATHS), redacted log excerpts (NZBLAB_LOGS), home network device list (NZBLAB_LAN). Service discovery (Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, SABnzbd, Tautulli, Overseerr/Jellyseerr) reads API keys from appdata read-only and hands them to the app over the token-protected API; Plex tokens are never read; turn it off with DISCOVER_KEYS=0. The agent never updates itself.
Network mode: the default Bridge works for everything. Only if you want the optional device list of your home network (NZBLAB_LAN=1) or the real network cards, switch Network Type to Host (optional) and then set Listen address to your server address. Without it, the agent only sees the Docker network.
After the first start, open the container log: the line "NZBLab-Agent Token: ..." appears once. Paste the token into the app (Settings, Server connections, NASlab-Agent). The token is also stored in appdata/nzblab-agent/token.txt. A read-only browser dashboard runs on port 8099 (HTTPS with a self-generated certificate: your browser warns once, compare the fingerprint shown in the container log). Setup window: the agent hands service API keys to the app only over HTTPS and only during the first 30 minutes after the first start. Set up the app within that time. Later (once keys were handed out), a restart no longer opens the window; create an empty file keys-unlock in the appdata folder to open it for 10 minutes. Do not expose this port to the internet; use a VPN (WireGuard, Tailscale) when away from home.
What leaves your server: no measurements, files or keys. The agent itself contacts only these addresses: 1.1.1.1 port 443, a plain connection test once a minute to measure internet latency (no data is sent; NZBLAB_NET=0 turns it off); disk price sites (Toppreise.ch, Geizhals, diskprices.com), only when a price country is set, with your own disk models as search terms (PRICE_SOURCES_OFF turns sources off); speed.cloudflare.com, only when you start a speed test in the app; and your ntfy server, only if you set NTFY_URL. Each of them sees your connection's IP address. The agent never sends data to the developer.
License: the agent is free and open source (GNU AGPL-3.0-only), source code on GitHub. The NASlab app is a separate, closed-source Android app (Google Play).
Deutsch: Misst Temperaturen, CPU, Grafikchip, RAM und Plattenzugriffe rund um die Uhr für die NASlab-App. Nur lesen, ändert nichts am NAS. Den Token zeigt das Container-Log beim ersten Start einmal, danach steht er in appdata/nzblab-agent/token.txt.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: nzblab naslab monitoring temperature smart disk spin-up android app
Container.Changes: 1.20.2: own user number 8099 (not shared with other containers), disks stay asleep (drivetemp read only for disks with activity), key window marker only after real output, fixed error texts, ntfy without redirects, empty template fields no longer stop the agent, home-network search only in private networks and on all interface names, history over 2 days averaged per 10 minutes, NAS name instead of container ID (optional path /host/etc/hostname), fixes for disk prices, file index and cache shares. 1.20.1: setup window opens at start only until service keys were handed out once (afterwards only via the file keys-unlock), HTTPS is only announced to the app when it really runs, AMD Ryzen: real chip temperature (Tdie) instead of Tctl, heat alert only after continuous minutes above the limit. 1.20.0: HTTPS on port 8099 (own certificate, fingerprint in the container log), plain HTTP can be switched off (NZBLAB_HTTP=0), service keys only over HTTPS in a 30-minute setup window after start (or 10 minutes after creating the file keys-unlock), new settings NZBLAB_TLS_SAN and NZBLAB_HTTP. 1.19.2: fixes and hardening, no new settings. 1.19.0: host check for /api/ping and /api/health (new setting NZBLAB_HOSTS for VPN or own domain names), shorter token errors, ntfy shows program names only to a server in your home network. 1.18.0: ntfy sends only critical alerts by default (NZBLAB_NTFY_ALL=1 for all), home network device search is off by default (NZBLAB_LAN=1 turns it on), syslog content only with NZBLAB_LOGS=1, security audit fixes. 1.17.0: sensor limits from hwmon, Synology disk names (sata1...), mover state from the system log (only with log excerpts on). 1.16.1: token hardening (min. 32 characters), crashes endpoint needs the token, parser limits. 1.16.0: service discovery (Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, SABnzbd, Tautulli, Overseerr) for one-step setup in the app. 1.15.0: reboot history, per-disk temperatures, RAID/pool status, network latency, backup discovery, optional SMART and log excerpts.
Container.Requires: The NASlab Android app (coming to Google Play soon, closed test until then: https://tuxxler.github.io/nzblab/en/#play). The agent runs on Unraid 6.12 or newer; the app needs Unraid 7.2 or newer for server control.

Config.Name: Web/API port
Config.Description: Port for the app and the browser dashboard

Config.Name: Data (/config)
Config.Description: Required, read/write. The agent stores its token and history here; without it you get a new token after every update. History (SQLite), file index, settings and token.txt. The only writable path.

Config.Name: Shares (file index)
Config.Description: Read-only. Search across all shares, storage analysis, duplicates, media inventory, appdata sizes. appdata, system, domains and isos are skipped by the index.

Config.Name: Cache pool
Config.Description: Read-only. What is waiting for the mover, per share. Remove this path if you have no pool named 'cache' (more pools: variable CACHE_ROOTS).

Config.Name: Host /sys
Config.Description: Read-only. Temperature sensors and GPU.

Config.Name: Host /proc
Config.Description: Read-only. CPU load, top programs, disk activity.

Config.Name: Host name file (optional)
Config.Description: Optional, empty by default. To show the name of your server instead of the container ID, set /etc/hostname (read-only).

Config.Name: Unraid notifications
Config.Description: Read-only. Unraid notifications for the 'Today' timeline.

Config.Name: System log
Config.Description: Optional, empty by default. To enable, set /var/log (read-only): errors from the syslog for the 'Today' timeline.

Config.Name: Docker container names
Config.Description: Optional, empty by default. To enable, set /var/lib/docker/containers (read-only): container names in the 'top load' list. Needs PUID=0 (the files are readable by root only). The files contain container environment variables; the agent only keeps the names.

Config.Name: WireGuard names (optional)
Config.Description: Optional extra path, empty by default. To show names of WireGuard devices, set /boot/config/wireguard (read-only). Those files also contain the server's private WireGuard key; the agent never passes it on, but the container could read it. Without this path only the names are missing.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User the agent runs as after start (8099 = its own number, not shared with other containers). 0 = root: needed only for container names and appdata folders of other containers with strict permissions.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group (100 = users)

Config.Name: Token (optional)
Config.Description: Best leave empty: the agent creates a random token on first start (container log and appdata/nzblab-agent/token.txt). If you set your own: at least 32 random characters, no spaces (shorter values are refused).

Config.Name: Heat alert (C)
Config.Description: Push via ntfy when the CPU stays above this temperature (Celsius) for 5 minutes

Config.Name: ntfy URL (optional)
Config.Description: e.g. https://ntfy.sh/a-long-secret-topic for push alerts while away

Config.Name: SMART (optional)
Config.Description: 1 = read SMART values of the disks (model, serial, power-on hours, reallocated/pending sectors, CRC/media errors, wear, temperature). Read-only: smartctl --scan and smartctl -a -n standby only, never self-tests, never writes, sleeping disks stay asleep. Needs the disks as devices and SYS_RAWIO, e.g. Extra Parameters: --cap-add=SYS_RAWIO --device=/dev/sdb (NVMe also --cap-add=SYS_ADMIN). Leave PUID as is: a small root helper only runs smartctl. 0 = off.

Config.Name: Log excerpts (optional)
Config.Description: 1 = the app may show recent error and warning lines from the System log path (/var/log, read-only). IP/MAC/e-mail addresses, tokens, passwords, user names and share paths are removed before anything leaves the agent; it never sends logs anywhere by itself. 0 = off.

Config.Name: Network latency
Config.Description: 1 = every minute, measure the TCP connect time to the router and to 1.1.1.1:443 (no data is sent, no extra rights). Shows in the app whether the router or the internet is slow. 0 = off.

Config.Name: Find services and API keys
Config.Description: 1 = the app can connect Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, SABnzbd, Tautulli and Overseerr/Jellyseerr in one step: the agent reads their API key, port and URL base from the settings files in appdata (Shares path, read-only; no docker.sock). Since agent 1.20: only over HTTPS and only in a setup window (30 minutes after the first start, until keys were handed out once; afterwards create an empty file keys-unlock in the appdata folder to open it again for 10 minutes; a token alone never unlocks). Value always = no window (not recommended). Only with the agent token, at most 10 requests per minute, never logged. Plex tokens are never read; Jellyfin/Emby keys must be created in their web UI. 0 = only list which services exist, without keys.

Config.Name: Allow plain HTTP
Config.Description: From agent 1.20 the agent speaks HTTPS on the same port (own certificate, created on first start; its SHA-256 fingerprint is in the container log and on the web page). 1 = plain HTTP stays on as well for older app versions (transition period). 0 = HTTPS only. Service keys and token renewal are never sent over plain HTTP.

Config.Name: Extra certificate names (optional)
Config.Description: Optional, empty by default. Comma-separated host names or IP addresses to put into the agent's own HTTPS certificate, e.g. the LAN address of the server (with bridge networking the container does not know it). Only used when the certificate is created, i.e. on first start (delete /config/tls/agent-cert.pem to create it again; the fingerprint then changes).

Config.Name: Backup paths (optional)
Config.Description: Comma-separated container paths of backup repositories (restic, borg, kopia) or backup log files (rsync, scripts), e.g. /host/backup. Add each one as an extra read-only path first. Only file names and times are read, never the backup contents. Empty = only search the shares for backup folders.

Config.Name: Home network devices (optional)
Config.Description: 0 = off (default). 1 = list the devices in your home network: every 30 minutes the agent sends one empty UDP packet to each address of your /24 network, reads the ARP table and asks the router for device names. New devices can be reported by push. A router or intrusion detection may report this as a port scan. Works best with Network Type Host.

Config.Name: ntfy: all messages (optional)
Config.Description: 0 = ntfy sends only critical alerts (disk failed, array stopped, CPU too hot); the app reports the rest. 1 = also send info messages (cheap disks, new devices, back to normal) and program names. Only has an effect when the ntfy URL is set.

Config.Name: ntfy: program names (optional)
Config.Description: 0 = program and container names ('top load') appear in ntfy messages only when your ntfy server is in your home network. 1 = also send them to a ntfy server under your own domain. Leave at 0 for ntfy.sh.

Config.Name: Extra host names (optional)
Config.Description: Comma-separated host names that may reach the agent, for VPN or your own domain (ZeroTier, WireGuard, reverse proxy), e.g. nas.example.org,.vpn.example.net. Exact name, or a leading dot for everything below it. IP addresses, localhost, names without a dot and .local/.lan/.ts.net work without this. Entries like * or .com are refused.

Config.Name: Listen address
Config.Description: Address the agent listens on inside the container. Keep 0.0.0.0 with bridge networking; use your server address with host networking, or 127.0.0.1 behind a reverse proxy.

Config.Name: Price country (optional)
Config.Description: Disk prices: CH, DE, AT, US, GB, ... Usually set from the app. Empty = no price lookups.
